blindingLimitation: The full brief was delivered together. This is a genuine image-led comparison, but not a formally blinded assessment of unseen calibration criteria.
inspectionMethod: Actual images interpreted through view_image; not metadata or metric inference.

differences.title: Landscape first, individual plants second
differences.referenceObservation: Large golden swathes read as connected fabric. Curving intermediate groups carry most of the field; thin strokes decorate a few crests and the close foreground.
differences.wildloomObservation: The retained field resolves into repeated little branching shapes, while the ribbon candidate resolves into separate spiky tufts. The middle clearing is a different, largely empty surface.
differences.aestheticConsequence: Attention jumps between thousands of equally insistent marks instead of reading a meadow as a few composed forms.
differences.principle: A hierarchy of silhouette/value masses, intermediate rhythms and subordinate detail must survive reduction.
differences.technicalHypothesis: Use a continuous grassland substrate and intermediate curved masses; reserve thin geometry for selected foreground and silhouette regions rather than covering the field with the same tuft.

differences.title: Illumination organizes the land into connected shapes
differences.referenceObservation: Warm lit bands and cool shaded bases sweep across many plants at once. Highlights are selective; the dark framing supports a luminous open middle rather than outlining every blade.
differences.wildloomObservation: The ground is a comparatively flat ochre area interrupted by sharp dark plant edges. Grass often has the same olive/gold response across large distances, while the sky has much richer soft tonal structure.
differences.aestheticConsequence: The eye gets strong local contrast but weak large-scale guidance and little sense of light flowing across the landscape.
differences.principle: Broad light/value relationships should dominate local material contrast.
differences.technicalHypothesis: Share a low-frequency world-space illumination/palette field between substrate and vegetation, retain the existing sun, and suppress high-frequency contrast away from selected lit crests.

differences.title: Directional rhythm replaces radial repetition
differences.referenceObservation: Long curved strokes lean through the foreground in related directions. Their groups bend around open areas and overlap, creating a rhythm rather than a visible planting pattern.
differences.wildloomObservation: Repeated radial fans and pointed clusters face many unrelated directions. Similar shapes repeat from close foreground to the distance; the ribbon alternative changes the object but retains the repetitive spiky rhythm.
differences.aestheticConsequence: The field feels assembled from objects instead of grown and swept into coherent movement.
differences.principle: Correlated directional variation at the group scale can unify many irregular local silhouettes.
differences.technicalHypothesis: Use a slowly varying lean/orientation field, overlapping curved surfaces and varied edge breakup; let individual blades diverge modestly from the larger flow.

differences.title: The clearing belongs to the grassland
differences.referenceObservation: Open regions transition through shorter, lower-contrast growth and exposed-earth variation. Neighboring grass bases share the ground's shadow color, and roots/bases disappear into a common surface.
differences.wildloomObservation: The central opening resembles an ochre stage surrounded by different, discrete geometry. Crisp dark bases and abrupt changes in visible plant height announce where objects begin.
differences.aestheticConsequence: The open encounter area reads as an exclusion mask rather than a naturally occurring part of the landscape.
differences.principle: Material, spatial coverage and height must express the same transition, including places with little geometry.
differences.technicalHypothesis: Drive terrain color, plant base color and a gradual height envelope from shared fields, with soft soil/vegetation transitions and restrained contact shading rather than isolated black bases.

differences.title: A common painterly language and depth hierarchy
differences.referenceObservation: Foreground sweeps, simplified middle bands, quiet cooler distance and a broad tree silhouette all use varied but compatible edges. The attractive sky and land feel painted with related decisions.
differences.wildloomObservation: The sky is soft and expressive, but grass remains hard-edged and similarly object-like over depth. A simple distant band and sharp foreground marks provide little intermediate visual structure. Puget's protected reference demonstrates a calmer, more continuous ground opening than the savanna.
differences.aestheticConsequence: The land looks pasted beneath the sky; objects compete across depth and the scene lacks an intentional visual rhythm.
differences.principle: Detail, contrast, edge softness and palette separation should change together with depth while retaining biome identity.
differences.technicalHypothesis: Use depth-aware simplification and quiet surface color at distance, medium-scale overlapping grass shapes nearby, and sparse native-scale detail. Keep sky/camera/tree systems fixed while testing whether the land can join their visual language.
